items.question: What kind of breath-control is recognized as the supreme form?
premises: That breath-control is devoid of something.
It is described as without embryo.
The wise know it as supreme.
items.inference: The supreme breath-control is the one that is devoid and without embryo.
items.plain_english: The wise know that supreme breath-control to be devoid and without embryo.

items.question: For how long is practice required to attain the highest quality?
premises: Attainment of the highest quality is the goal.
Practice is undertaken for that attainment.
Practice is desired as long as that attainment is not complete.
items.inference: Practice should continue until the highest quality is attained.
items.plain_english: Practice is to be pursued as long as the attainment of the highest quality is desired.

items.question: How is pratyāhāra defined as a prescribed yogic practice?
premises: Pratyāhāra involves withdrawal.
This withdrawal is from them, meaning sense objects.
The withdrawal is done by force and is prescribed.
items.inference: Pratyāhāra is prescribed as the forceful withdrawal of the senses from their objects.
uncertainties: The referent of 'tebhyaḥ' is contextually taken as sense objects.
items.plain_english: Pratyāhāra is prescribed as the forceful withdrawal from them.

items.question: What practice is declared to constitute dhāraṇā in this teaching?
premises: Dhāraṇā is being defined.
It involves holding.
The object held is the breath-wind.
items.inference: Dhāraṇā is declared to be the holding of the breath-wind.
items.plain_english: The holding of the breath-wind is declared to be dhāraṇā.

items.question: What is identified as dhyāna in the context of this practice?
premises: Dhyāna is being defined here.
It involves meditation on desired deities.
This meditation takes place in the self.
items.inference: Dhyāna is called the meditation on desired deities within the self.
items.plain_english: Here, meditation on the desired deities within the self is called dhyāna.

items.question: What do the sages declare about samādhi in relation to the eight limbs?
premises: The sages make a declaration about samādhi.
Samādhi is described as having the characteristic of eight limbs.
This characterization has been previously declared.
items.inference: The sages declare samādhi to be characterized by the eight limbs.
items.plain_english: The sages declare samādhi to be that which is characterized by the eight limbs.

items.question: What teaching does the speaker now promise to explain to the listener?
premises: The speaker addresses the listener directly.
The speaker announces a new topic now.
The topic is the unsurpassed mantra-yoga.
items.inference: The speaker now promises to explain the unsurpassed mantra-yoga.
items.plain_english: Now I shall tell you about the unsurpassed mantra-yoga.

items.question: How are the principal channels distinguished and ranked in this account?
premises: Among them ten are declared chief.
Among those, three are established.
This indicates a hierarchy among the channels.
items.inference: Ten channels are chief, and among them three are especially established.
uncertainties: The referent of 'tāsu' is contextually taken as channels (nāḍīs).
items.plain_english: Among them, ten are declared chief, and among those, three are established.

items.question: How do the sages describe the appearance and name of the viṣa channel?
premises: A channel is remembered by the sages.
It is named viṣa.
It resembles the filament of a pomegranate.
items.inference: The sages remember the viṣa channel as resembling a pomegranate filament.
items.plain_english: The sages remember the channel named viṣa as resembling a pomegranate filament.

items.question: What essential nature and form are attributed to the suṣumnā channel?
premises: The suṣumnā is being described.
She consists of all light.
She has many forms.
items.inference: The suṣumnā is all-light in nature and many-formed.
items.plain_english: She, the suṣumnā, indeed consists of all light and has many forms.

items.question: What is the extent of this channel from visarga to bindu in reality?
premises: This entity extends spatially.
Its lower limit is the emission point.
Its upper limit is the drop.
items.inference: In reality, this stands extending from the emission point up to the drop.
uncertainties: The referent of 'etat' is contextually taken as the suṣumnā.
items.plain_english: In reality, this stands from the emission point up to the drop.

items.question: What is located in the middle and what is its radiant splendor?
premises: Something is located in the middle.
It is the self-born liṅga.
Its splendor equals that of ten million suns.
items.inference: In the middle is the self-born liṅga, radiant like ten million suns.
items.plain_english: In the middle is the self-born liṅga, with splendor equal to ten million suns.

items.question: What is the form and nature of kuṇḍalī located above that point?
premises: Kuṇḍalī is located above that.
She is shaped like a flame.
Her form is that of brahman.
items.inference: Above that, kuṇḍalī is flame-shaped and has the form of brahman.
items.plain_english: Above that is kuṇḍalī, flame-shaped and having the form of brahman.

items.question: What should the practitioner visualize there and with what appearance?
premises: A visualization is prescribed there.
The object of visualization is a lotus.
The lotus appears like molten gold.
items.inference: One should visualize there a lotus resembling molten gold.
items.plain_english: There one should visualize a lotus with the appearance of molten gold.

items.question: Which lotus is identified by the six letters from ba to la and named ādhiṣṭhāna?
premises: A lotus is associated with six letters.
The letters range from ba to la.
This lotus is named ādhiṣṭhāna.
items.inference: The lotus joined with the six letters from ba to la is named ādhiṣṭhāna.
items.plain_english: Joined with the six letters beginning with ba and ending with la, it is named ādhiṣṭhāna.

items.question: Why do the wise know this center as svādhiṣṭhāna in relation to the supreme liṅga?
premises: The supreme liṅga is associated with the sound sva.
This association gives rise to the name svādhiṣṭhāna.
The wise know it accordingly.
items.inference: Because of the sound sva associated with the supreme liṅga, the wise know it as svādhiṣṭhāna.
items.plain_english: Because of the sound sva, the wise know the supreme liṅga as svādhiṣṭhāna.

items.question: Why is that lotus called maṇipūra according to its described quality?
premises: That lotus is being described.
It is pierced like a jewel.
Because of this it is called maṇipūra.
items.inference: That lotus is called maṇipūra because it is pierced like a jewel.
items.plain_english: That lotus, pierced like a jewel, is thus called maṇipūra.

items.question: What presiding power and causal status are attributed to this lotus?
premises: The lotus is presided over by Śiva.
It is described as the sole cause of all worlds.
These attributes define its significance.
items.inference: The lotus presided over by Śiva is the sole cause of all worlds.
items.plain_english: The lotus, presided over by Śiva, is the sole cause of all the worlds.

items.question: What letters and petals are said to preside over this lotus center?
premises: The lotus is associated with specific letters.
The letters range from ka to ṭha.
It is also associated with twelve petals.
items.inference: This lotus is presided over by the letters from ka to ṭha and by twelve petals.
uncertainties: 'arka+patraiḥ' is interpreted as twelve petals by traditional association of arka with twelve.
items.plain_english: It is presided over by the letters beginning with ka and ending with ṭha, and by twelve petals.

items.question: What name do the sages celebrate for that particular lotus center?
premises: That lotus is being identified.
The sages celebrate its name.
Its name is anāhata.
items.inference: The sages celebrate that lotus as named anāhata.
items.plain_english: That lotus is celebrated by the sages as named anāhata.

items.question: What names and qualities are attributed to the viśuddha lotus center?
premises: The lotus is called viśuddha.
It is also named after ether.
It is described as greatly wonderful.
items.inference: The viśuddha lotus is called ether-named and greatly wonderful.
items.plain_english: The lotus is called viśuddha, named after ether, and greatly wonderful.

items.question: What is said to occur at that center regarding the guru's command?
premises: Something occurs there at that center.
It involves the transmission of command.
This is identified as the guru's command.
items.inference: There occurs the transmission of command, celebrated as the guru's command.
items.plain_english: There the transmission of command is celebrated as the guru's command.

items.question: What has been declared to the listener regarding the śiva-cakras?
premises: The speaker addresses the listener as virtuous one.
The śiva-cakras have been described.
This description has now been declared to the listener.
items.inference: Thus the śiva-cakras have been declared to you, O virtuous one.
items.plain_english: Thus, O virtuous one, the śiva-cakras have been declared to you.

items.question: What is stated to be located above that as the place of the bindu?
premises: A location above that is being described.
It is the place of the bindu.
It is identified as the thousand-petaled lotus.
items.inference: Above that, the thousand-petaled lotus is stated to be the place of the bindu.
items.plain_english: Above that, the thousand-petaled lotus is stated to be the place of the bindu.
